metas.name: Canada - 45° angle transformers
metas.note: Transformers on Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia will be installed at a 45° angle relative to the road. On PEI, red numbers will usually be written on the side.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Alberta bollards
metas.note:
Alberta has a unique black and white bollard that is often found at intersections. It has a cylindrical shape and two black bands that wrap all the way around. It is one of the most useful Canadian bollards to learn because it appears so frequently.

NOTE: Some Alberta bollards have a yellow band between the two black bands, instead of a white one. Blue bands can also rarely be seen, particularly in and around Calgary, while green bands are rarely seen in and around Edmonton.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Alberta license plates
metas.note: Alberta license plates has red text on white background, it shows up as a red tint in the blur. It can be hard to see and it takes some time to get used to spotting it. Front plates are NOT required. Note: New Brunswick has similar license plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - British Columbian speed limit signs
metas.note:
Some provinces have unique speed signs.

British Columbian signs include the ‘km/h’ but lack the black section in the Ontario sign.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Concrete barriers
metas.note: British Columbia predominantly uses concrete barriers instead of guardrails.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Exposed rocks
metas.note: The Canadian Shield extends through the eastern part of Canada. Therefore, you will commonly see exposed rocks on street view in the highlighted area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Green and white striped sticker
metas.note: You can sometimes find a green and white striped sticker on signposts in Manitoba.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Manitoba bollards
metas.note:
Manitoba uses black and grey painted bollards. Most of the time an orange stripe will be present below the grey one.

Wooden, rectangular bollards of this form are typically found further north in Manitoba

NOTE: Bollards in this format with just a black top are seen in Manitoba and Saskatchewan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Manitoba license plates
metas.note: Manitoba license plates has green on both sides. Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland bins
metas.note:
Bins made of wood planks can be seen on Newfoundland driveways. These are most commonly octagonal, however they can have other shapes.

NOTE: Although they are most common in Newfoundland, they can also sometimes be seen in other provinces, such as New Brunswick.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland fire hydrant markers
metas.note: Fire hydrants in Newfoundland often have a diamond-shaped marker next to them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario diamond-shaped markers
metas.note: You can find these diamond-shaped markers on the sides of the roads in Ontario. The colours can vary.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario KM markers
metas.note: Ontario KM markers have a white square at the bottom, which is unique to the province.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario pole tops
metas.note:
These distinctive pole tops are most commonly found in Ontario. They have two insulators to the side, and one on top. The side insulators are affixed to the pole with a distinct attachment. Sometimes, multiple of them can be stacked on top of each other.

NOTE: They can occasionally appear in British Columbia, Nova Scotia, or other provinces more rarely.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario speed limit signs
metas.note:
Some provinces have unique speed signs.

Ontario speed limit signs may have a black section on the bottom with the words ‘km/h’ or ‘begins’ written in white.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario traffic cones
metas.note: Ontario uses distinct orange and black striped traffic cones.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario wooden guardrail posts
metas.note: In Ontario, you will often see these types of guardrails. They consist of cylindrical wooden posts, held together by precisely three metal wires. Some posts are marked by a reflective white band.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Prince Edward Island red soil
metas.note:
Prince Edward Island soil has a distinct red tint to it. Potato farming is also very common on PEI.

NOTE: This type of soil can occasionally be seen in certain areas of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Québec bollards
metas.note: Québec has unique bollards that are always attached to guardrails. They are long, thin white poles with a red or green reflector at the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Québec fire hydrant markers
metas.note:
You will often find these yellow fire hydrant markers atop signposts in Québec.

In Québec City these markers will usually have a blue rectangle and markers in Trois-Rivières are distinctly small.

NOTE: Sometimes the markers will have different colours. Beware that Edmundston, in New Brunswick, uses these too.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Québec French speed limit signs
metas.note:
Some provinces have unique speed signs.

Québec can sometimes have French on their speed limit signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Québec poles
metas.note: Some Québec poles have recognizable pole tops with insulator rods that are angled slightly upwards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Québec traffic cones
metas.note: Québec has unique orange and white striped traffic cones.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan alternating insulators
metas.note: Pole top insulators in Saskatchewan alternate. While one pole will have one insulator on the left and two on the right, the next will have two on the left and one on the right.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan license plates
metas.note: Saskatchewan license plates has green text on white background, it shows up as a green tint in the blur. It can be hard to see and it takes some time to get used to spotting it. Front plates are NOT required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Stop and Arrêt signs
metas.note:
Stop signs with both ‘Stop’ and ‘Arrêt’ are most commonly found in New Brunswick.

NOTE: Such stop signs can rarely be found in other provinces.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Transformers facing the road
metas.note: The transformers on poles will face the road in British Columbia and New Brunswick, while in other provinces, it will be parallel with the wires.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - White triangles on signpost
metas.note: Signposts in Saskatchewan can feature these white triangles. The number can vary.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Wooden post pyramid top
metas.note: In Newfoundland and Labrador, most wooden posts on guardrails have this pyramid shaped top. Occasionally, you can spot them on standalone posts and signposts as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: United States - Agricultural golden fields
metas.note:
Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington.

NOTE: Flat areas of northern and eastern Oregon can have a similar appearance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Alabama license plates
metas.note: Front plates are NOT required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Alaska license plates
metas.note:
There are three variants of Alaska license plates.

  1. A yellow background with black text
  2. A background that is blue on the top, white in the middle and yellow on the bottom.
  3. A background that is blue on the top and white on the bottom with a bear in the middle and red text.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Alaskan highway shield
metas.note: The Alaskan highway shield has an image of the Big Dipper constellation on the bottom left.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Arizona license plates
metas.note: Front plates are NOT required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Black between middle lines
metas.note: A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - California Central Valley
metas.note:
Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.

In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - California utility poles
metas.note: Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Colorado license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Concrete highways
metas.note:
Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.

NOTE: Concrete paving on residential streets is commonly seen throughout the Midwest states and parts of the East Coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Connecticut license plates
metas.note: Connecticut license plates are blue on top and fades into white on the bottom. Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Corn fields
metas.note: Corn fields can most commonly be found in these regions. For a detailed overview, see this map.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Cotton
metas.note:
Cotton is a crop that produces large fields of fluffy white flowers. It is most commonly produced in coastal Southeast States, the Lower Mississippi River Valley, Western Texas, and parts of California and Arizona. You can click here for a more detailed map.

NOTE: When cotton is not fully grown (earlier in the year) cotton fields often look like image number 2.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Delaware license plates
metas.note: Delaware license plates has gold text on dark blue background, it shows up as a dark blue blur with gold in the middle, and is easy to spot. Front plates are NOT required. Note: A similar plate can be found in Michigan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Diamond bollards
metas.note:
The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.

NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Double signpost
metas.note:
Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.

NOTE: Double signposts can also be seen in other states, but are not as common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Douglas firs
metas.note:
Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana.

Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Eastern white pine
metas.note:
The Eastern white pine (Pinus strobus) is a large pine native to eastern North America. It can be found in the Great Lakes region and in the Appalachian Mountains.

Image source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/nrs/atlas/tree/v3/129
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Florida license plates
metas.note: Florida license plates has green text on a white background, and it has oranges in the middle, which makes the plate unique. Front plates are NOT required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Georgia license plates
metas.note: Front plates are NOT required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Hanging traffic lights and signs
metas.note:
Many large intersections in Michigan have stop lights and signs that hang from wires that stretch across the middle of the intersection. These markers are commonly in yellow boxes.

NOTE: These are not completely unique to Michigan, but are most commonly seen there.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Hawaii license plates
metas.note: Hawaii license plates has black text on a white background. It also has a rainbow in the background that is somtimes more or less visible. Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Hawaiian language
metas.note:
Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used. Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.

Hawaiian is a vowel-oriented language that only uses eight consonants: H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and (ʻ), called an ʻOkina.

Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U.

Each vowel can also have a macron over it: Ā, Ē, Ī, Ō, and Ū.

These vowels are often combined to make Diphthongs. I.e. UI, AI, AE, etc...
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Hawaiian topography
metas.note: Topography on Hawaii is characterised by many sloping volcanoes, rugged cliffs, hills, valleys and craters. Such distinct topography combined with tropical vegetation is a good way to identify Hawaii.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Idaho license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Illinois license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Indiana license plates
metas.note: Front plates are NOT required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Kansas white reflectors
metas.note: These white reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas. They are most commonly seen on ‘stop’ signs in rural areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Maryland license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Massachusetts license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Minnesota black-and-white marker
metas.note: On most rural ‘stop’ signposts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is attached to the posts horizontally. The shape may vary slightly.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Minnesota yellow signs
metas.note: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Nebraska Sandhills
metas.note: The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Nevada Bollards
metas.note: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Nevada license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - New Hampshire license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - New Jersey license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - New Mexico license plates
metas.note: New Mexico license plates has red text on yellow background or yellow text on green background, it shows up as a mostly yellow or green blur, and is easy to spot. Front plates are NOT required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - New York license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - No middle line
metas.note:
Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.

NOTE: This can rarely be seen in other states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - North Dakota license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Oil pumpjacks
metas.note: Oil pumpjacks are short, industrial-looking metal structures located at the surface of oil fields and are used to pump crude oil from the earth below. They are most common in western states, particularly in Texas, Eastern New Mexico, and North Dakota.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Oklahoma license plates
metas.note: Front plates are NOT required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Oregon license plates
metas.note: Oregon license plates has blue text on white background with a green tree in the middle, it shows up as a green dot in the white/blue blur on the sides. Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Prairie potholes
metas.note: The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many ‘prairie potholes.’ These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Red mesas and tablelands
metas.note: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Red soil
metas.note: Many parts of the Deep South, stretching from Oklahoma to South Carolina, have reddish soil. The exact tint of the soil can range from yellow to deep red.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Rice
metas.note:
Rice production only occurs in a few areas of the US, so it is very useful for region guessing. It is typically grown in large, flat fields that resemble low prairies. It is only grown in north-central California and the Lower Mississippi River Valley in Arkansas, Louisiana, Texas, and Mississippi. You can click here for a more detailed map.

NOTE: When rice is not fully grown, rice fields often look similar to image 2.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Sagebrush
metas.note: Great Basin Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata) is a short, shrubby blue-green bush that is common in the interior western United States.It is most common in arid areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Saguaro cacti
metas.note: Saguaro cacti are most commonly shaped like tall, straight tubes with several branches extending from the main tube. They are most commonly found in southern Arizona, on the Sonoran border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - South Dakota license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Southern pines
metas.note: The loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), and longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), commonly referred to as southern pines in the community, are found throughout the southeastern US. They are a great way to recognize this region, as they are abundant, recognizable and mostly limited to this part of the country. They tend to be tall, with fluffy-looking clusters of pine needles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Soybeans
metas.note: Soybeans are short, dark green crops organised in long rows and are found in similar regions where corn is grown. They are most common in the Eastern Plains, Midwest, Lower Mississippi Valley, and areas of the Mid Atlantic.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Spanish moss
metas.note: Spanish moss, appearing as greyish white drapes, can sometimes be seen on trees in the deep south.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Speed instead of Speed Limit
metas.note: Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word ‘Speed’ instead of the standard ‘Speed Limit’.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Temperate rainforests
metas.note:
Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.

NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Texan roads
metas.note:
Texan roads often have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface.

NOTE: Similar pavement can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Texas license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - The Great Basin
metas.note:
The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains.

The tallest mountains are in Nevada, Utah and California. More gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon, and greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah.

Keep in mind that there are exceptions, so make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - The Rocky Mountains
metas.note: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Thick road lines
metas.note:
Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland use middle yellow lines that are thicker than traditional yellow road lines.

NOTE: These are not present on all roads in these states, and can be found elsewhere, so use this tip in conjunction with other clues.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Utah license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Vermont license plates
metas.note: Vermont license plates has white text on green background, it shows up as a green blur with white on the sides, and is easy to spot. Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Washington bollards
metas.note: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Washington license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Wide middle lines
metas.note:
Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon. They can also be found to a lesser extent in Washington, Alabama, and Michigan.

NOTE: Wide middle lines can also rarely appear in other states, so consider other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Wisconsin ATV Route signs
metas.note: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Wisconsin bollard
metas.note: These simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Wisconsin pole plate
metas.note: A rectangular white metal plate, with an orange rectangle and diamond, can be seen on most poles in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Wyoming license plates
metas.note: Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Yellow or red bands
metas.note:
Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas.

NOTE: Similar reflectors can sometimes be seen in other states, such as Hawaii.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.
